articles.title: Stan Stan who? Rishabh Pant joins local Christchurch game, goes on six-hitting spree - India Today
articles.summary: Stan Stan who? Rishabh Pant joins local Christchurch game, goes on six-hitting spree India Today
articles.content: Rishabh Pant is clearly not one to let a cricket bat gather dust, even between Test matches. Ahead of India's second Test against New Zealand, the wicketkeeper-batter found himself playing a rather unexpected game of cricket in Christchurch, turning a casual invitation into a 21-ball blitz.Pant, listed as Stan Stan on the scorecard, joined the Open House Swingers for a Last Man Stands match against The Chosen Ones at Hagley Park on Wednesday. The India star smashed 54 off just 21 deliveries, including a handful of sixes, keeping his explosive batting touch intact ahead of the Test, which begins Friday.The outing came after a chance encounter in central Christchurch, where Open House Swingers player Mohammad Safi spotted Pant riding an electric bike. What followed was an invitation that turned into a memorable evening for the local cricket team."I saw Rishabh going around on an electric bike," Safi told the New Zealand Herald. "So I went and stopped him, and we start talking and taking a few photos and stuff, and I asked him, do you want to play cricket for us?"Pant apparently didn't need much convincing."He was like, OK, I'll come and play for you guys. Then he came and padded up, went batting, and smashed a few sixes," Safi recalled.A QUIRKY ALIASThe appearance was apparently low-key enough for Pant to go unnoticed by the opposition initially. Safi said the India star was wearing a striking blue tracksuit and was not immediately recognised by the players on the other side.Pant also didn't arrive with his own cricket equipment. According to Safi, the wicketkeeper-batter used his cousin's bat during the game, but that hardly stopped him from making an impact.The 29-year-old's knock was another reminder of his penchant for attacking cricket. Pant has established himself as one of the most prolific six-hitters in Test cricket, with 108 maximums across 53 matches, placing him second on the all-time list.He had already showcased that ability during India's first Test against New Zealand in Wellington, where he struck six sixes in a memorable innings of 128 off 153 balls. India went on to post 720-9, setting a record total in New Zealand, although the match eventually ended in a draw.Pant's Christchurch cameo was not entirely about keeping his batting rhythm intact. It also offered a glimpse of the personality that has made him one of the more entertaining figures in international cricket.COACHES SURPRISEDPant's impromptu appearance even caught members of the Indian team off guard. Bowling coach Morne Morkel admitted he was taken aback when he learnt about the wicketkeeper-batter's local cricket adventure."I nearly fell off my chair last night when I saw that," Morkel said.New Zealand captain Tom Latham, meanwhile, was delighted by Pant's willingness to join a local side and share his cricketing experience."He's obviously a real character of the game is Rishabh, so it's great for him to give his experience back to the LMS teams," Latham said.The Open House Swingers eventually won the match by 16 runs, adding another unusual chapter to Pant's Christchurch visit.The India wicketkeeper-batter will now turn his attention to the more familiar surroundings of Hagley Oval, where India and New Zealand are set to resume their Test battle on Friday. But before stepping back into the international spotlight, Pant managed to squeeze in a little local cricket, a few big hits and an evening that the Christchurch players are unlikely to forget anytime soon.- EndsMust Watch

articles.title: Can't destroy ecosystem for development, Bombay HC warns Maharashtra govt - India Today
articles.summary: Can't destroy ecosystem for development, Bombay HC warns Maharashtra govt India Today
articles.content: The Bombay High Court on Wednesday raised concerns over damage to the ecosystem caused by development projects and stressed the need to balance environmental protection with rapid urbanisation, news agency Press Trust of India reported.A bench of Chief Justice Mahesh Chandra Tripathi and Justice Advait Sethna said Maharashtra government agencies could not treat tree plantation as a paperwork formality while clearing green cover for urban infrastructure.The court was hearing a petition filed by the Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority through advocate Saket Mone, seeking permission to divert 0.2869 hectares of mangrove forest land for a transport project.The approval is required to build an 8.85-km elevated Automated Rapid Transit System, a driverless electric pod car network, at Mumbai's Bandra-Kurla Complex. The commercial district has faced traffic congestion for a long time.The court said authorities must make advance efforts towards afforestation instead of first seeking permission to clear mangroves and leaving ecological restoration for later.The bench noted that planting saplings, which may or may not grow into full-sized trees, was not serving the intended purpose.“Why damage the ecosystem? The efforts of replantation have to be sincere and genuine. Once we give permission, then efforts are taken for plantation. That would take years,” the court observed, according to PTI.The bench said development projects affect full-grown trees and mangroves, which are salt-tolerant shrubs or trees that grow along tropical shores, while the saplings planted in their place take years to mature.“There has to be a balance in the ecosystem. We are disturbing the ecosystem on account of development. Development is also important. But the rehabilitation of the environment has to move simultaneously. Permission is accorded today, but it would take five to ten years for the tree to grow. Right now we are disturbing the ecosystem,” the court said.In its petition, the state-run MMRDA claimed that no mangroves would be cut for the project. It said six trees would be affected and assured the court that it would plant 100 trees as compensation.Mone told the court that the elevated corridor was vital for last-mile connectivity in the busy business district. The bench questioned why compensatory measures had not been initiated when the project was conceived.Maharashtra Advocate General Milind Sathe said a shortage of suitable saline land delayed mangrove plantation. He maintained that saplings were planted before the monsoon to ensure their long-term survival, PTI reported.The court directed the state government to submit concrete data from the past five years on total green cover, losses and sapling survival rates before it passed an order. It scheduled the next hearing for November 30.The High Court reiterated that development and environmental rehabilitation must proceed together and sought detailed data before deciding on the MMRDA's request to divert mangrove forest land for the transport project.- EndsMust Watch

articles.title: Gurnoor Brar knocking on the door: Morkel weighs in on pacer's inclusion for 2nd Test - India Today
articles.summary: Gurnoor Brar knocking on the door: Morkel weighs in on pacer's inclusion for 2nd Test India Today
articles.content: India bowling coach Morne Morkel has acknowledged the excitement surrounding Gurnoor Brar, hinting that the young pacer could be well suited to the conditions ahead of the second Test against New Zealand in Christchurch, even as he stressed the importance of being ready when an opportunity comes.Gurnoor, who is yet to make his Test debut, has made a strong impression during the ongoing tour of New Zealand. The Punjab-born pacer was among India's standout performers in the five-match ODI series, finishing as the leading wicket-taker despite featuring in only three matches.The 2000-born pacer claimed nine wickets at an average of 15.89, showcasing his ability to generate pace, hit hard lengths and extract movement off the seam. His performances against New Zealand's batters have strengthened the case for him to be considered as India look to bounce back in the second Test.Speaking ahead of the upcoming match, Morkel acknowledged the promise Gurnoor has shown since joining the Indian set-up and suggested that the conditions could suit his bowling style."With Gurnoor, I mean, there's a lot of excitement about him since he joined the Indian team with his pace and bounce. I think he's a guy that will be well suited to the conditions here," Morkel said.KNOCKING ON THE DOORGurnoor has been pushing for a place in India's Test side, with his performances on the tour giving the team management another option to consider in the pace department. However, Morkel was careful not to suggest that an inclusion was imminent, underlining the importance of the young bowler being prepared for the demands of Test cricket."Gurnoor has been knocking on the door. He is doing all the right things. But again, he needs to just make sure he's ready when he gets the opportunity," the India bowling coach said.Morkel added that a bowler can sometimes get caught up in the anticipation of a debut or a place in the playing XI, and that his responsibility would be to ensure Gurnoor is fully prepared when the moment arrives."As a bowler, you can get distracted. When he gets his opportunity, my job is to make sure he's 100 per cent ready when he gets that opportunity," he added.India's bowling attack has come under scrutiny following the previous Test, where the team was unable to convert a commanding batting performance into a victory. India piled up more than 700 runs in the first innings but struggled to dismiss New Zealand's batters on a surface that offered little assistance to the bowlers.The pace attack, led by Jasprit Bumrah and featuring Prasidh Krishna, Akash Deep and Anshul Kamboj, had limited opportunities to make an impact as the conditions remained largely batter-friendly. The inability to take all 10 wickets despite a substantial first-innings total has raised questions about whether India could benefit from another pace option.Gurnoor's pace and ability to extract bounce could offer a different dimension, particularly if the conditions in Christchurch provide greater assistance to seamers. His ODI performances have certainly made him a player to watch, although the final call on his inclusion will depend on the team management's assessment of the conditions and balance.FOCUS ON THE TASKWith India facing a challenging task in the upcoming Test, Morkel also urged the players to shut out external noise and concentrate on executing their plans rather than getting caught up in the pressure surrounding the series.The bowling coach acknowledged that reaching the final Test with a chance to compete for the series would be a difficult proposition, but insisted that the team would continue to give everything in pursuit of that goal."All these guys want to play in that final Test and they will give everything possible to make it. But realistically, if we are honest about it, it is going to be a challenge," Morkel said.He stressed that India needed to avoid allowing setbacks or difficult sessions to dictate their approach, instead focusing on finding solutions and playing their best cricket."After every bad session, we can't get caught up in things that we need to do. We just need to focus on playing our best cricket, coming up with solutions, and from there take it forward," he said.Morkel said the team would look to break the contest down into smaller phases, with an emphasis on staying focused and building momentum session by session.For Gurnoor, meanwhile, the message remains clear: keep doing the right things, stay prepared and wait for the opportunity to make his mark in Test cricket.- EndsMust Watch

articles.summary: Fadnavis urges Maharashtra citizens to share their views on Uniform Civil Code by Dec 15 The New Indian Express
articles.content: Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis has appealed to citizens to share their views on the Uniform Civil Code (UCC) by December 15, asking them if they think a common framework of civil laws should apply to every citizen residing in the state.In July this year, the state government set up a seven-member committee headed by retired Supreme Court Justice Ranjana Desai to draft a framework for implementing the UCC, which seeks to establish equal laws across religions on issues of marriage, divorce, and property.The panel launched an online questionnaire and has been holding public consultations and hearings in the state..Maharashtra govt plans to table UCC Bill in winter session: CM Fadnavis.In a post on X made through the Chief Minister's Office (CMO) handle, Fadnavis said the committee is seeking citizens' views on implementing the UCC in the state."Do you think a common framework of civil laws should apply to every citizen residing in Maharashtra? The committee invites your views, perspectives and suggestions on the implementation of the Uniform Civil Code in Maharashtra," he said.Fadnavis said the appeal is to individuals, government agencies, NGOs, social groups and communities, religious bodies and political parties to share their views on UCC.maharashtra.gov.in or email to ucc@maharashtea.gov.in.The post also explained that the UCC proposes a common framework of civil laws for all citizens irrespective of religion.Earlier this month, Fadnavis defended his government's decision to draft the UCC, asserting that the Constitution itself directs states to work towards its implementation.Prior to that, he had said the law would be introduced in the upcoming winter session or the next budget session of the state legislature.The winter session will be held in Nagpur from December 7 to 18.(With inputs from PTI).Former Justice RC Chavan quits Maharashtra UCC panel, cites differences over functioning.UCC to be implemented across India, government committed, says Meghwal.Follow The New Indian Express channel on WhatsApp Download the TNIE app to stay with us and follow the latest

articles.content: CHENNAI GYMNASTICS Services, UP strike gold as gymnasts dazzle at Youth Nationals on Day One The opening day of the inaugural Youth Artistic Gymnastics National Championships at INS Hamla, Malad, saw Services and Uttar Pradesh emerge as the early frontrunners, clinching the Grade 7 Out-Age and In-Age team titles, respectively. The day’s proceedings began with the Grade 7 Out-Age competition, where Services demonstrated remarkable consistency and depth across the apparatus to amass 146.866 points and finish atop the team standings. West Bengal mounted a spirited challenge to secure second place with 144.732, while Tripura completed the podium with 136.267. The individual all-around final provided one of the day’s closest contests, with Services’ Sudip Ghosh and West Bengal’s Tanmoy Maitra finishing locked on an identical score of 51.834. Sudip, however, was adjudged the winner, leaving Tanmoy to take the silver. Services’ Dnyaneshwar completed the podium with 51.199 points. Dnyaneshwar proved a picture of strength and composure on the apparatus, showcasing his upper-body power and control to capture two individual titles. He scored an impressive 9.833 on the Still Rings before following it up with 8.933 on the Parallel Bars. Sudip, meanwhile, brought grace and fluidity to his Floor Exercise routine, earning 9.800 to claim the title. Tanmoy displayed his versatility by dominating the Pommel Horse and Horizontal Bar events to walk away with both crowns. The Vault final witnessed a rare dead heat, with Haryana’s Gautam and Telangana’s Mohammad Murtaza Jeelani sharing the top honours after both registered 9.200 points. The spotlight then shifted to the Grade 7 In-Age competition, where Uttar Pradesh produced a commanding collective performance to top the team standings with 157.034 points. West Bengal stayed hot on its heels with 156.330, while Maharashtra finished third with 150.867. Maharashtra’s Snithik Patil emerged as the star of the individual all-around competition, displaying an impressive blend of agility, strength and technical finesse across the apparatus to accumulate 56.300 points and secure the title. West Bengal’s Suprit Chanda finished a worthy runner-up with 54.832, while Uttar Pradesh’s Manash Singh claimed third place with 53.333. Snithik carried his rich vein of form into the apparatus finals, producing a polished Parallel Bars routine that combined fluid transitions with impeccable control to score 9.867 and add another gold to his collection. Suprit, too, enjoyed a memorable outing, soaring to the Horizontal Bar title with 9.300, while Karnataka’s Agasthya Bellam Konda showcased his prowess in the Vault to top the event with 9.333. The gymnastics action moves to the men’s Grade 8 competition on Day 2. The men’s events will continue until November 26, before the senior and junior men’s selection trials take centre stage on November 27. articles.title: Maharashtra govt amends 2016 university Act, empowers chancellors to remove pro-VCs | Mumbai news - Hindustan Times
articles.summary: Maharashtra govt amends 2016 university Act, empowers chancellors to remove pro-VCs | Mumbai news Hindustan Times
articles.content: Chancellors of private universities in Maharashtra can now remove Pro-Vice-Chancellors (Pro-VCs) on the recommendation of vice-chancellors, following an amendment to the Maharashtra Public Universities Act, 2016, through an ordinance.The ordinance, promulgated by the state higher and technical education department on Monday, amends Section 13 of the Act, which earlier empowered a university’s Management Council to remove a Pro-VC on the recommendation of the Vice-Chancellor and on specified grounds. The amendment transfers this authority to the Chancellor.“... As the Pro-Vice-Chancellor is higher rank academic and executive officer of the university next in rank to the Vice-Chancellor, it is considered expedient to provide that the Pro-Vice-Chancellor may be removed by the Chancellor instead of by the Management Council, on the recommendation of the Vice-Chancellor. It is, therefore, proposed to amend section 13 of the said Act, suitably,” the ordinance said.The vice-chancellor is the principal academic and executive officer of a university and heads its various authorities, bodies and committees. The Pro-VC, who has jurisdiction over the entire university, is next in the hierarchy and presides over these bodies in the absence of the vice-chancellor.“The changes are part of amendments to the Maharashtra Public Universities Act, which provides the framework for academic autonomy, democratic representation and regulation of higher education in the state,” a senior official from the higher and technical education department said.An ordinance can be promulgated to amend legislation when the state legislature or Parliament is not in session and immediate legislative action is required. It is issued by the governor on the recommendation of the state cabinet and has the same legal force as an Act passed by the legislature.However, an ordinance must be placed before the legislature when it reconvenes. It ceases to operate six weeks after the legislature reassembles unless approved by both Houses.

The Pro-VC, who has jurisdiction over the entire university, is next in the hierarchy and presides over these bodies in the absence of the vice-chancellor.“The changes are part of amendments to the Maharashtra Public Universities Act, which provides the framework for academic autonomy, democratic representation and regulation of higher education in the state,” a senior official from the higher and technical education department said.An ordinance can be promulgated to amend legislation when the state legislature or Parliament is not in session and immediate legislative action is required. It is issued by the governor on the recommendation of the state cabinet and has the same legal force as an Act passed by the legislature.However, an ordinance must be placed before the legislature when it reconvenes. It ceases to operate six weeks after the legislature reassembles unless approved by both Houses.

articles.title: Maharashtra govt to introduce tougher law against exam malpractices during winter session: Fadnavis | Education - Hindustan Times
articles.summary: Maharashtra govt to introduce tougher law against exam malpractices during winter session: Fadnavis | Education Hindustan Times
articles.content: Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis on Tuesday said the state government will strive to introduce and pass a tougher law against examination malpractices during the upcoming assembly session, following new panel recommendations on test reforms and candidate fee refunds.The winter session will take place at Vidhan Bhavan in Nagpur from December 7 to 18.₹10-crore fine, stricter jail terms for exam malpractice">MPSC paper leak: Panel recommends ₹10-crore fine, stricter jail terms for exam malpracticeSpeaking to reporters here, Fadnavis said, "We have received another report from the committee constituted under the leadership of Radhika. Regarding examination fees, they have recommended that candidates should pay the fees to ensure seriousness, but once they appear for the examination, the fees should be refunded so that no one bears any financial burden.""To make the law that we had enacted earlier more stringent, they have recommended a stricter law. Our endeavour will be to introduce this law during this very session, if possible, and get it passed in the same session," the CM added.Bihar CM Samrat Choudhary directs completion of university infrastructure projects by March 2027Separately, brushing aside talk surrounding Nationalist Congress Party (Sharadchandra Pawar) chief Sharad Pawar stepping away from public life, Fadnavis pointed to the veteran leader's continued involvement in public works."It is the wish of all of us that Sharad Pawar Saheb enjoys good health. Pawar Saheb is active even today and having observed him closely, I have seen that he consistently takes an interest in various projects and works. Therefore, it is not appropriate to discuss his retirement. I am confident that he will never stop in his lifetime," he said.Earlier on Monday, Fadnavis met Nandan Nilekani, Chairman of the High-Powered Task Force constituted to strengthen security, introduce reforms and ensure transparency in the examination process, according to Maharashtra CMO.Why should students attend college lectures when AI can teach them? BITS Pilani VC V. Ramgopal Rao answersFormer ISRO Chairman S Somanath and senior officials were also present.Earlier in July, Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced the formation of the task force under technology expert Nandan Nilekani to recommend measures for strengthening the examination system, amid protests over alleged irregularities in the NEET-UG 2026 examination and paper leaks.PM Modi said the task force would submit a report and stressed the need for a "reliable" and "transparent" examination system with greater use of technology.In a video message on X, the Prime Minister said, "The Government of India is continuously taking various measures for the future of students. Those who tampered with the students' future are languishing in jail. We have already established fast-track courts. We are also moving towards enacting new legislation in Parliament that incorporates stringent legal provisions. However, we must look to the future. Our examination system needs to be reliable and transparent, and it must make maximum use of technology.""Keeping all these factors in mind, we have decided to constitute a high-powered task force under the leadership of the world-renowned technology expert Nandan Nilekani. This task force will focus on examination reforms, and based on its report, steps will be taken to ensure the credibility of upcoming examinations at the earliest," he added.The Nandan Nilekani task force will comprise a multidisciplinary group of experts tasked with suggesting measures to revamp examinations conducted by the National Testing Agency (NTA), with a focus on technology integration and structural reforms.The other members of the high-powered task force include former ISRO Chairman S Somnath, former Intelligence Bureau Director Tapan Deka, IIT Madras Director V Kamakoti, former Education Secretary Anita Karwal and logistics expert Amrit Lal Meena. (ANI)
